ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended), especially Articles 2(1)(13) and 5-2 on customer and beneficial owner identification; Enforcement Decree of the same Act; Financial Services Commission Regulation on Customer Identification and Verification; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality (Act No. 5493, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended); Foreign Investment Promotion Act; and Supreme Court Corporate Registration Rules. Beneficial ownership information is collected and held by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and reporting institutions; there is no public UBO register for a Yuhan Hoesa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Corporate Registration Extract of the parent entity or post-incorporation Korean Yuhan Hoesa corporate registry extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the jurisdiction of issuance; in Korea, the Supreme Court of Korea commercial registry district court office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: FOR HAGUE STATES: issuance by the registry followed by apostille issued by the state's designated competent authority under the Hague Apostille Convention; stop there. FOR NON-HAGUE STATES: issuance by the registry, authentication by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then consular legalization by the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that state; stop there. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternative channels and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Legal Entity Existence or No-Litigation Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of corporations or tax authority in the state of the parent or ultimate beneficial owner; in Korea, the National Tax Service and the district court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, the certificate must be apostilled by that state's competent authority only. If the issuing state is not a party to the Convention, the certificate must be authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that issuing state only. The two routes are mutually exclusive and cannot be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney of the Parent or Ultimate Beneficial Owner authorizing the formation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or sole corporate member of the parent entity, notarized by a public notary in the state of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization first, then either (i) apostille by the Apostille Convention competent authority if the state of execution is a Hague member, or (ii) local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication followed by Korean consular legalization if the state of execution is not a Hague member. Never use apostille and consular legalization in sequence for the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Articles of Association (Jang-gwan) of the proposed Korean Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public in the district court jurisdiction of the Korean registered office, prepared by licensed Korean counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use inside Korea no apostille or consular legalization is required. If the notarized Korean Articles must be produced abroad, obtain a Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille for Hague destination states; for non-Hague destination states obtain consular legalization by the destination state's mission in Korea. The channels are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / private bank KYC and introduction letter for the beneficial owner and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Private bank or regulated financial institution where the beneficial owner maintains the funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on bank letterhead; notarize the bank officer's signature, then apostille by the origin state's Hague Apostille Convention competent authority if the origin is a Convention member; if the origin is not a Convention member, notarization followed by local foreign ministry authentication and Korean consular legalization is required. Apostille and consular legalization must not be stacked.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, signatories, directors, and family-office principals must undergo enhanced due diligence before incorporation: mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's domestic financial sanctions list; PEP identification covering domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs, their family members, and close associates; real-name verification under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act; source of funds and source of wealth analysis; adverse media review; jurisdiction risk review; risk rating; and continuous transaction monitoring. Any positive hit, unexplained wealth, or false disclosure must be escalated to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and must result in refusal of formation services. Minimum 60 words satisfied.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (IRO / Internet Registration Office; iRO.go.kr) name-search and corporate registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered company name must be entered in the Korean corporate register in Hangul. A foreign-language trade name may be used as a secondary name, but the Korean legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa must appear. The recommended four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinctive Hangul brand identifier or a stable Korean phonetic transliteration of a foreign brand; (2) a descriptive business-activity segment, such as family office investment and assets management; (3) the statutory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (4) an optional separately registered English trade name. Transliteration must be accurate, non-deceptive, and sufficiently distinct to avoid identical-name misidentification in the same registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Administrative or governmental designations such as National, Government, Presidential, or agency names requiring prior authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the iRO name search rejects a proposed name because of an identical or misleadingly similar existing name or a sensitive token, the applicant should first amend the proposed name and submit a new online search. For a rejection of a provisional trade-name registration, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the appellate court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure within two weeks of the registry decision, using the district court that issued the refusal and attaching evidence of distinctiveness and the corrected name. If the issue is the use of a sensitive financial token, the applicant must first obtain prior ministerial approval or written authorization from the Financial Services Commission; if denied, the denial may be challenged by administrative litigation before the Seoul Administrative Court. A provisional name reservation in Korea is valid for 180 days and may be re-filed after expiration if incorporation is not completed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or post-office mailbox is not permissible as the sole registered office for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa because the National Tax Service and the Court Registry require an actual business place address with capacity for service of process and tax notices. However, a lawful serviced office with a physical Korean address, lease, meeting-room access, and a local administrative representative may satisfy the statutory registered-office requirement. For the ISIC 6430 single-family-office scope, private banks providing private-banking wire and securities custody will generally reject a mailbox-only profile and will expect the company to show local decision-making substance, accounting records, and an identifiable office operator in Korea.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced municipal tax or registry inspection: (1) visible company sign at the registered address; (2) access to corporate seal and books; (3) Korean resident director or licensed fiduciary provider available; (4) board minutes documenting investment policy decisions made in Korea; (5) bank-managed source and use of funds; and (6) absence of nominee-led shell indicia. Quantified risk: approximately 35-45% annual inspection probability for a virtual-office-only investment holding company, reducing to below 15% for a genuine serviced office with a local manager and contemporaneous corporate records. A Yuhan Hoesa that files a business registration and maintains a proprietary discretionary family-office mandate is subject to National Tax Service audit selection and municipal property-visit checks, so registered-office substance must be maintained.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 543 through 553 (Yuhan Hoesa), together with the Registration of Real Estate Cases Act as applied to commercial registration and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (electronic filing via the I-Plus Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa (title: law-in-lai-seong-gi), accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and capital deposit certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. The capital amount set forth in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully subscribed and, for non-resident subscribers, remitted in foreign currency to a domestic bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; domestic subscribers may pay by deposit into a provisional bank account in the company's name. No blocked escrow account is required for domestic-only shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby constitute the corporation as a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, and that the duly subscribed capital of One Hundred Million Korean Won (KRW 100,000,000) shall be paid in full by each subscriber in proportion to the number of quotas subscribed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Articles of Incorporation presented to this first meeting be, and they hereby are, adopted as the sole and binding organic documents of the company, and that the officers of the corporation are directed to execute, notarize, and file the Articles of Incorporation and all ancillary instruments with the District Court Registry Office and the National Tax Service without delay. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the company shall be established and maintained at 10th Floor, Hanwha Building, 110 Jongno-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, within the territorial jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court, and that the company is authorized to open, maintain, and operate corporate deposit, securities custody, and foreign currency accounts at one or more domestic commercial banks, with signing authority vested in the Representative Director jointly with any other director as required by banking practice. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons be and hereby are appointed as statutory officers for the first fiscal year: (a) Kim Min-jae as Representative Director and internal director; (b) Park Soo-ah as Auditor, to serve in accordance with Article 547 of the Commercial Act; and (c) Lee Joon-ho as agent for service of process in the Republic of Korea. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Representative Director and any one director, acting jointly, are authorized to execute and submit all incorporation documents, to pay all official fees, to sign all agreements with banks and securities custodians, and to take every lawful step necessary to complete the formation and registration of the company, to obtain the corporate business registration and tax identification number, to file the foreign investment report with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy if any shareholder is a non-resident, and to make such corporate elections and registrations as may be required for the single-family-office purpose of the company, which is limited exclusively to managing the assets and investments of the founding family and shall not include providing investment advisory services to third parties. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are expressly instructed to maintain the shareholder ledger, minutes of general meetings, corporate seal register, and accounting records in accordance with the Commercial Act, and to commission an external audit if the company meets the asset or revenue thresholds under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, as applied mutatis mutandis to Yuhan Hoesa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Articles of Incorporation Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-Plus) at www.iros.go.kr and the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search through the I-Plus corporate name database to confirm that the proposed entity name, KR_YUHANGHOESA, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing domestic corporation. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean with mandatory contents: company name, business purpose limited to a single-family office and private holding of family assets, address of the registered office, total capital amount, number and type of quotas, method of contribution, and the names of the incorporators. Engage a Korean-licensed attorney to review the business-purpose clause so that the company does not inadvertently hold itself out as an investment advisory or collective investment business requiring authorization under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.
required_dossiers: Company name search report from I-Plus
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Passport or ID copies of all incorporators
Proof of address for non-resident directors
Legal opinion on business scope restriction to own-family assets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search reveals a conflicting or similar name, select a distinctive alternative name and resubmit the search; if the registry queries the business purpose as potentially regulated, submit a supplemental legal opinion clarifying that the activities are restricted to the family's own asset management and do not extend to third-party advisory services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public commissioned within the jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All incorporators must appear before a notary for authentication of the Articles of Incorporation, evidenced by a notarial certificate affixed to the articles. Each subscriber shall execute a written quota subscription certificate stating the number of quotas subscribed and the amount contributed. For cash contributions, the subscribers shall deposit the paid-in capital into a domestic bank account held in the name of the corporation under a provisional incorporation account, and obtain a capital deposit certificate indicating the company as the account holder and the subscribed amount. If contributions are to be made in kind, a licensed appraiser's valuation report must accompany the articles. After notarization and deposit, the incorporators must convene by subscribed vote to approve the articles and formally resolve to proceed with the incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Quota subscription certificates signed by each subscriber
Capital deposit certificate issued by the bank
In-kind contribution valuation report, if applicable
Corporate seal (dojang) registered specimen
Passport or ID of each subscriber and director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies discrepancies in signatures or subscription amounts, correct the subscription certificates and have the affected pages re-notarized; if the bank refuses to issue the capital deposit certificate because the provisional account name is incomplete, request the bank to reissue the certificate with the exact corporate name as written in the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Division through the I-Plus Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within three weeks of the notarization date, submit the application for incorporation registration of the Yuhan Hoesa to the competent court registry. The application must be filed on the prescribed registration form and may be filed electronically through I-Plus, accompanied by the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, the capital deposit certificate, a power of attorney if filed by a licensed attorney, and identification copies of the directors and auditor. The court will verify the legality of the incorporation, confirm payment of registration tax and local education surcharge, and, upon approval, issue a certificate of registered matters (deung-gi-sa-hang-jeon-bu-jeung-myeong). The corporate legal personality is effective as of the date the court completes the registration.
required_dossiers: Application for Incorporation Registration (court-prescribed form)
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit certificate
Power of attorney, if filed through an attorney
Passport copies of directors and auditor
Corporate seal specimen certificate or registration card
Payment receipt for registration tax and education surcharge
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a notice of suspension or correction, the applicant must cure the specified defect within the period stated in the notice and refile through I-Plus; if the court refuses registration, the applicant may apply for an immediate appeal to the district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act or file a new application after rectifying the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Identification Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the HomeTax online portal or the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days of the completion of court registration, file for the corporate business registration certificate (sa-eop-ja-deung-rok-jeung) under the Corporate Tax Act and the Value-Added Tax Act. Submit the certificate of registered matters issued by the court, a certified copy of the corporate seal registration, the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the lease agreement for the registered office, and the identification of the representative director. The National Tax Service will issue a corporate tax identification number, register the company for value-added tax filing, employee withholding, and electronic tax invoice issuance. If any shareholder is a non-resident, the company must also file a foreign-investment report with KOTRA and obtain a foreign exchange bank receipt for the remitted capital, which serves as a precondition for the tax office's acceptance of certain foreign currency transactions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered matters (deung-gi-sa-hang-jeon-bu-jeung-myeong)
Corporate seal certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease agreement and landlord's consent
Resident ID and corporate seal of representative director
Foreign investment report and exchange bank receipt, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office holds the registration for lack of verifiable office evidence, present a certified rental contract and a utility bill in the company's name; if a non-resident shareholding is queried, provide the completed foreign-investment report and a letter from the foreign exchange bank confirming capital remittance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Banking and Regulatory Compliance Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, Financial Services Commission (only for verification of non-applicability), Financial Information Analysis Institute for beneficial ownership reporting, and the bank's compliance department for account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, convene the first formal board meeting to adopt this pro-forma resolution, officially appoint the Representative Director, and authorize the opening of operating bank accounts, securities custody accounts, and, if needed, foreign currency accounts. The Representative Director must apply for corporate seal certificates and submit attestation of beneficial ownership to the financial institution under the Financial Transaction Reports Act. The company must also maintain the shareholders' register and an accounting ledger reflecting the opening balance sheet. For a single-family office exclusively owning family assets, no financial regulatory license is required; however, the company should obtain a written legal opinion from a Korean financial law attorney confirming that its activities do not constitute asset management, investment advisory, or brokerage for third parties. Additionally, if the company leases office premises, the lessor's approved building occupancy certificate must be kept on file.
required_dossiers: First board resolution minutes (this pro-forma resolution)
Certificate of corporate seal registration
Copies of directors' passports or resident IDs
Office lease agreement and occupancy certificate
Beneficial ownership declaration forms required by the bank
Written legal opinion on non-applicability of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank delays or rejects account opening based on anti-money-laundering review, elevate the matter to the bank's compliance officer with full shareholder and director identification, source-of-wealth documentation, and the legal opinion confirming the single-family-office character; if the beneficial ownership filing is rejected by the Financial Information Analysis Institute, refile with a corrected ownership chart and certified translations of shareholder records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — the entity is a private single-family office engaged in ISIC 6430 (trusts, funds and similar financial entities) and will not operate physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facilities under ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no industrial or sectoral operating license is required because the company restricts its activities to holding and investing the founding family's own high-net-worth assets and does not provide services to third parties; if future scope expansion occurs, a separate license under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act would be assessed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea — Not Applicable to a pure office-based holding entity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical project requiring a full EIA report or environmental registration is proposed; the company will occupy a standard office lease with no construction or land alteration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — no industrial discharge, VOC emission, hazardous waste generation, or significant resource usage arises from the single-family-office activity. The company will nonetheless comply with ordinary indoor air quality and waste segregation obligations of the Seoul metropolitan district, and any office renovation must conform to indoor air quality standards under the Indoor Air Quality Control in Public Facilities Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a separate permit — no civil-defense fire certificate is required for a non-hazardous office use; the lessor must possess and maintain a valid building occupancy certificate and fire-safety inspection approval under the Fire Prevention, Fire-Fighting and Emergency Rescue Act. The company must install basic fire extinguishers, maintain unobstructed egress paths, and comply with the general duties of employers under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for its staff, including a workplace safety inspection at the leased office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr). Export clearance and customs audit: Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa Korean LLC: (1) incorporate under the Korean Commercial Act and obtain the corporate registration certificate from the competent court registry; (2) file a foreign investment report through KOTRA/Invest Korea or an authorized foreign exchange bank and retain the Foreign Investment Report Certificate; (3) within 20 days of business commencement, file Business Registration with the district tax office through the HomeTax portal, attaching the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, foreign investment report certificate, lease or proof of ownership for the Korean registered office, the representative director's identity documents, and a power of attorney if a tax representative is appointed; (4) the National Tax Service will then issue a 10-digit Business Registration Certificate, and that Business Registration Number simultaneously serves as the corporate tax identification number and VAT registration number; (5) a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean place of business that must file Korean VAT, for example for digital services supplied to Korean consumers, must appoint a domestic tax representative and apply for a foreign business operator VAT registration number through HomeTax, providing notarized and apostilled foreign incorporation documents, board resolution, and the tax representative's power of attorney; this foreigner registration does not automatically create a permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election. A Yuhan Hoesa is per se a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed at the entity level; it cannot elect pass-through treatment. No hybrid mismatch election exists, and hybrid mismatch outcomes are adjusted mandatorily under the Act on Adjustment of Taxes of International Transactions. The only tax-group election available is the Korean consolidated corporate filing regime for a resident parent with wholly owned resident domestic subsidiaries, and that regime does not alter the separate legal or tax classification of the Yuhan Hoesa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No statutory turnover threshold in KRW for corporations; VAT registration is mandatory upon business commencement under Article 5 of the VAT Act, and the 10-digit Business Registration Number constitutes the VAT registration. Simplified taxable person status is available only to individual business operators with annual taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80 million, and a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC does not qualify for that simplified regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All tax invoices must be issued as mandatory e-Tax Invoices under Article 32 of the VAT Act and transmitted to the National Tax Service through the HomeTax e-tax invoice system no later than the day after issue, unless the transaction is a B2C cash receipt eligible for the real-time cash receipt mechanism. The taxpayer's ERP/accounting system must transmit the e-tax invoice data through the NTS-certified XML/API channel or the HomeTax web portal; Korea does not operate a pre-clearance digital stamping model. Anti-fraud integrity is achieved through mandatory sequential e-tax invoice transmission, NTS data matching, automated VAT return reconciliation, and, for B2C cash transactions, real-time cash receipt device transmission to NTS. Late, false, or non-transmitted e-tax invoices trigger VAT Act penalty taxes and, for intentional falsification, criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export supplies under the Korean VAT Act include goods physically exported from Korea to foreign countries; services supplied to a foreign country or to a non-resident where the place of supply and actual consumption are outside Korea; international maritime and air carriage of goods or passengers; and other foreign-currency-earning supplies prescribed by Presidential Decree. Offshore digital services qualify for 0% VAT when the recipient is a non-resident, the service is not legally or practically consumed in Korea, and the consideration is paid in foreign currency to a Korean bank account. Any service consumed or used in Korea is subject to the standard 10% VAT even if invoiced to a foreign person, so a single family office must evidence the overseas place of benefit to substantiate zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Electronic Export Declaration approved in the UNI-PASS export clearance system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the goods description, quantity, and export value
Foreign Exchange Bank Confirmation of Foreign Currency Settlement or Receipt (inward foreign exchange remittance certificate) issued under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Bank statement or Foreign Exchange Information System (FES) record showing that the export proceeds were received and settled in Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subjected to NTS matching with UNI-PASS customs declarations, bank foreign exchange records, and e-tax invoice data. If the customs export declaration, bill of lading, or foreign exchange receipt is missing, mismatched, or insufficient to trace the shipment to the repatriated payment, the NTS rejects the 0% rate and reassesses VAT at the standard 10% on the export consideration, with statutory interest from the original VAT filing date under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Penalty tax is additionally imposed for the issuance of false e-tax invoices or for fraudulent VAT refund claims under the VAT Act, and intentional manipulative export refund schemes are prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, which carries imprisonment and fines up to the statutory evaded-tax multiples. Retrospective clawback can extend up to ten years for fraudulent refund activity, and the assessed VAT, penalties, and interest are collected through national tax enforcement and asset seizure procedures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Ministry of Economy and Finance delegated foreign exchange administration protocols
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea applies a liberalized but supervised foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions are effectively freely convertible and are subject to post-verification by domestic foreign exchange banks, while capital account transactions require filing or declaration with the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Foreign direct investment, investment in private equity funds, and share subscription transmissions for a single family office are classified as capital account transactions; they must be filed through a domestic bank with Know-Your-Customer documents and the underlying investment contract. Gross proceeds from liquidation, dividends, and interest may be repatriated after tax clearance, but banks require evidence of the initial foreign investment registration and the report of the transaction in the Foreign Exchange Information System. No surrender requirement exists for inbound or outbound remittances, but all cross-border transfers above USD 5,000 per transaction must be reported to the bank for monthly transmission to the Bank of Korea. The main convertibility hurdles are not administrative in terms of conversion but documentary: a UBO with heavy beneficial ownership concentration, unexplained family wealth from prior digital export receipts, and insufficient proof of economic substance for the holding entity all serve as de facto blockers. Practical convertibility is High once the entity has opened a corporate currency account and established an approved FIPA foreign investment registration number, allowing full conversion of USD into KRW and repatriation in USD without surrender for a single family office. A single-family office is expressly not a licensed financial company, and it avoids the Foreign Exchange Concentration Base System, but the restriction on CIKs may create a payment rail bottleneck. Overall, South Korea permits convertibility subject to robust FIU reporting, true economic-beneficiary disclosure, and demonstrable underlying assets, making it a transparent, upper-band OECD jurisdiction with no centralised blacklist risk.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected within one year from the date of export declaration, extendable to three years with Bank of Korea approval for capital goods export, and zero percent are required to be surrendered; the full amount may be credited to a foreign currency account held with a licensed domestic foreign exchange bank. Once credited, conversion to KRW is optional. All receipts must be settled through a domestic designated foreign exchange bank and filed in the bank's official settlement records to satisfy the export proceeds repatriation timeline.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account / Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Account for NDF and forward transactions
Basic Operational Currency Account / Private Banking Liquidity Hub
Secondary operational current account for trade settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and non-resident electronic money institutions are legally barred from servicing a domestic corporate treasury in South Korea without a banking business license under the Banking Act and an Electronic Financial Business Provider registration under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. Foreign EMIs such as Mercury, Intergiro, or Airwallex cannot hold KRW clearing accounts, cannot issue local IBANs, and cannot perform cross-border FX brokerage with the Bank of Korea's payment system. The only viable path for fintech-style rails is through a domestic licensed bank's open banking APIs, so the overall feasibility rating is Low for offshore EMIs. Domestic online banks like Toss Bank operate under full banking licenses but focus on retail and do not offer the multi-currency account structure required for a single family office, making them impractical for private investment holding and securities custody.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean Financial Supervisory Service compliance guidelines, combined with the customer identification requirements under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions, require that the entity's statutory representative and at least one senior owner, or the delegated attorney-in-fact, appear for an identification interview. For non-resident directors, an in-branch interview at a Tier-1 bank is mandatory for the first KRW business account. Remote consular proxy opening is not a blanket right; it is permitted only when a notarised power of attorney issued by a Korean consulate is accompanied by a video interview and a notarised board resolution specifically authorising the proxy. In practice, at least one individual with actual signatory authority must be physically present in Seoul for final biometric capture before the account can be activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a single-family trust with layered ownership and no registration in Korea's Securities and Exchange Commission
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Color passport copies, foreign entity registration extracts, trust deed with settlor and beneficiary schedule, family relationship certificates, birth certificates for exercised beneficiaries, and a written consent to be included in the bank's customer register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from Hong Kong, Cayman, or a parent entity without documents proving the source of wealth of the family assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three years of audited financial statements of the originating entity, bank statements showing the complete liquidity trail, notarised purchase and sale contracts for the disposed assets, tax payment receipts, independent valuation reports, and a source-of-wealth declaration signed by the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Yuhan Hoesa has no employees and holds only investment assets, presenting shell company risk under Korean AML regulations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Appointment of a domestic outsourced accounting firm as AML outsourcing officer, lease agreement for an executive office, manager contracts, portfolio statements from major brokerages, custody balance certificates from KSD or OTC, and a business plan showing the family office's investment mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctions-listed counterparties or cryptocurrency-tainted digital content gaming revenues with an ambiguous blockchain trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transactional ledger with KYC for every counterparty, list of clearing references showing MT103 inbound numbers, IP licensing contracts, game publishing agreements, VAT invoices, and a negative-media screening report from an independent due-diligence vendor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a single-family office foreign direct investment, the family office will wire USD or KRW via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's account abroad to an escrow account at KB Kookmin or Hana Bank. The bank applies the appropriate Bank of Korea Foreign Exchange Information System settlement-purpose code for direct investment capital increase based on the FIPA notification. The entity must first submit the foreign investment notification to the bank or through KOTRA's Invest Korea portal, obtain a foreign investment registration number, and open the escrow account with foreign investor status. After share issuance, the bank issues a compliant capital verification certificate with the received amount and date. Inbound remittances should include field 70 with the FIPA notification number to ensure the Bank of Korea surveillance system automatically classifies the credit as direct investment rather than domestic borrowing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements, the family office will rely on SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments, commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed by a Korean Tier-1 bank, and documentary collections with sight or usance drafts. Each disbursement must be supported by the export licence, invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration if trade-related. For investment-related outflows, the bank requires an executed securities purchase agreement, a valuation statement, and the original foreign investment registration certificate to satisfy the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/KRW deliverable FX forward contracts with licensed domestic banks, limited to 100 percent underlying economic exposure from securities purchases, trade settlement, or dividend repatriation
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only when matched with long-term foreign currency borrowing or physical securities positions, with no naked speculative use

BOK-regulated non-deliverable forwards available only through domestic designated FX bank brokers for KRW hedging of non-deliverable assets, with minimum ticket sizes and real underlying transaction dossiers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Members' Meeting Resolution Approving Financial Statements and Register of Members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Members; corporate minute book retained at registered office under Korean Commercial Act Art. 611
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year fiscal year ending December 31, the meeting must be held by March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting is not directly strike-off, but all resolutions requiring member approval become invalid; continued neglect of corporate formalities may authorize the Court to order judicial dissolution under Korean Commercial Act Art. 176 at the request of any shareholder or the Public Prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return with Audited/Unaudited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surtax: 20% of unpaid corporate tax; overdue interest: 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum) calculated from the original due date; if a taxpayer fails to file for 6 months, NTS may seize bank accounts and impose a court-ordered delinquency disposition; continued non-return for 1 year triggers forced notice plus registration of serious violation, but not administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report (Substantive; DART Submission)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via DART (Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; if a certified auditor is appointed, the final opinion must be submitted to FSS within 2 weeks of the auditor's report being granted to the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain and file an external audit report within the statutory window is a criminal offense under the Act on External Audits; the company is subject to a fine up to 500,000,000 KRW (approx. USD 384,600) and the audit report for the next fiscal year must be filed as an audit exemption requalification; the Financial Supervisory Commission may ask a court for judicial dissolution if false or incomplete audit filings persist for two consecutive years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Review and Confirmation of the Membership Register (UBO Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of Yuhan Hoesa; changes in membership filed with the District Court Corporate Registry of the company's seat
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Register must be compiled as at fiscal year-end and confirmed at the annual members' meeting; each membership transfer must be registered with the court within 30 days of the transfer (Korean Commercial Act Art. 608)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration of a membership transfer subjects the company to non-contentious registration penalties up to 1,000,000 KRW (approx. USD 770) and restores the counterparty right; the company cannot assert a transfer electively against a third party until the registration is complete; repeated non-registration may be treated as concealment of beneficial owner for anti-money laundering enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Corporations, mandatory independent certification is triggered for any Yuhan Hoesa (including an ISIC 6430 Single Family Office) if: (a) total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million) at the fiscal year-end; (b) total debts exceed KRW 7 billion (approx. USD 5.4 million) and annual revenue exceeds KRW 30 billion (approx. USD 23 million); or (c) the entity is classified as a public interest entity (listed, financial company, or securities/asset-management company) regardless of size. Headcount trigger: average number of employees for the fiscal year exceeds 300. The audit must be performed by an independent certified public accountant registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants, and the opinion must be rendered under K-IFRS or K-GAAP in accordance with the rules of the External Audit Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for all external audit mandatory companies; Korean GAAP (business accounting standards) and SME GAAP for non-public Yuhan Hoesa not required to apply K-IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not require an annual UBO return to a government agency for a Yuhan Hoesa, but the company must maintain a Membership Register at the registered office. At each annual members' meeting, the register is reviewed for accuracy as of the fiscal year-end. Any transfer of membership interest must be approved by the members' meeting and applied for court registration within 30 days, and this filing is the effective legal method of recording beneficial ownership. Financial institutions performing customer due diligence may require a certified copy of this annual confirmation and an updated UBO/beneficial owner representation at least once every 12 months.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per year for a Seoul-based corporate service provider or virtual registry agreement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 45,000 per annual audit engagement for a single family office that crosses the statutory threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top progressive bracket plus 10% local income tax surcharge (aggregate 26.4%) for taxable income above KRW 300 billion; lower brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory family-office tax holiday; general incentives include R&D tax deductions, SME income-reduction provisions, foreign-investment tax reductions under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, and free-zone corporate tax exemptions; for a modest single-family-office profit of KRW 200 million, the effective national rate is 9% (9.9% with local surcharge) absent credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1 (Corporate Tax Return) plus attached schedules; mandatory electronic filing via the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr) or authorized e-filing softwares.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for a December 31 year-end); filing extension may be applied, but interest on late payment continues to accrue on unpaid tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business registration number, fiscal year-end, head office address, and statement of domestic or foreign controlling ownership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the entity as a resident Korean corporation and fully identify the ultimate non-resident shareholder or foreign trust in the accompanying ownership schedule; failure to disclose foreign control voids the ordinary correction facility and exposes the filer to inaccurate-return penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Statement of Profit or Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating and non-operating revenue, expenses, and net income prepared under K-IFRS or statutory accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korea-source income attributable to the domestic business place; a Korean domestic corporation must also include foreign-source income in worldwide income. Cross-border related-party transactions must be separately listed on the attached International Transactions Statement and reconciled to the source documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting income to taxable income through non-deductible expenses, non-taxable income, and statutory reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reclassify payments lacking economic substance (e.g., management fees paid to an offshore family trust without supportable functions, assets, and risks) as constructive dividends to the non-resident shareholder; this triggers 22% dividend withholding tax and may be adjusted under international tax rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of eligible net operating losses brought forward from prior years to compute the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify the 15-year carryforward availability and business continuity; an indirect transfer of 50% or more of the entity as a result of a non-resident trust restructuring may limit the deduction unless the same business is demonstrably continued.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Tax Computation, Credits and Preparatory Taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax at progressive rates, application of foreign tax credits, tax abatements, and deduction of prepaid taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim the foreign tax credit for Korean dividend withholding on the SFO's own Korean return; the credit belongs to the shareholder's local tax authority. Attach evidence of any taxes withheld on prior distributions and proof of treaty-eligible ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing: 20% of the unpaid tax as a negligence penalty. General underreporting: 10% of the understated tax; fraudulent underreporting: 40% of the understated tax. Overdue payment incurs 0.022% per day. Failure to file the International Transactions Statement separately attracts an additional penalty under the International Tax Adjustment Act, and willful concealment can escalate to criminal tax-evasion prosecutions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding on dividends plus 2% local income tax surcharge) unless reduced by an applicable bilateral income tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain and deliver a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, execute a Beneficial Ownership Declaration confirming the recipient is the true owner and not a conduit, and file the Application for Tax Treaty Reduction/Exemption with the Korean withholding agent before or by the payment date; the withholding agent must attach the approved forms to its withholding tax return. If tax has been over-withheld, a refund claim must be made within three years from the statutory payment deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge) for both interest and royalties. Treaty rates vary by jurisdiction; commonly 10% for interest and 10%–15% for royalties under Korea's network DTA, subject to beneficial ownership substantiation and no Korean permanent establishment connection.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 50 million for the annual International Transactions Statement; KRW 5 billion of cross-border related-party transactions for the Local File; KRW 100 billion group consolidated revenue for the Master File (as applicable under the International Tax Adjustment Act).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations registration, but substance is enforced through statutory anti-abuse doctrines, the beneficial ownership rules in the Income Tax Act, and Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act which disregards contracts whose legal form does not reflect economic reality. A single-family office must demonstrate actual economic presence through office premises, local board decisions, identified employees, and Korean-based custody and portfolio management; otherwise treaty benefits can be denied and investment income recharacterized as Korean-source business income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Unreported Offshore Investment Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting from the SFO's books interest, dividends, and capital gains on overseas securities custody accounts held through a related foreign trust; filing the corporate tax return with suppressed income and false asset declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax when the concealed amount exceeds KRW 300 million; plus 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty and daily overdue surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil under Article 401 of the Commercial Act for willful misconduct or gross negligence; directors can be held personally liable for unpaid corporate tax and penalties under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act, face overseas travel blacklisting and asset seizures, and may be sentenced to criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation / Round-Trip Fee Arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive cross-border management, consulting, or license fees to a non-resident related family trust with no employees and no operational control; failing to prepare or store transfer pricing documentation and excluding the fees from the International Transactions Statement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service adjusts taxable income to the arm's length price under Article 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act; disallowed fees attract corporation tax, 10% ordinary underreporting penalty, and a documentation penalty under Article 11 of the same Act; interest accrues daily.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the sham fee structure breach fiduciary duty and are liable for civil restitution under Article 401 of the Commercial Act; if the arrangement is found intentional, directors may also face criminal tax-evasion charges and joint liability for tax deficiencies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Default on Outbound Distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident beneficiary or foreign trust without withholding 22% tax and without filing a claim for DTA relief; failing to obtain the Tax Residency Certificate and Beneficial Ownership statement before the payment date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is liable for the unwithheld tax under the Income Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes; a 10% penalty on the un-withheld amount is imposed, plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest, and a separate penalty for failure to submit the withholding return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally and jointly liable for withheld taxes collected but not remitted, under Article 39 of the National Tax Collection Act; personal assets may be seized, travel restrictions enforced, and diverting withheld tax may constitute criminal embezzlement under Article 355 of the Korean Criminal Code.
